sources.name: The Clear Quran (Dr. Mustafa Khattab), islamicstudies.info
sources.excerpt: This Medinian sûrah deals with an incident that happened within the Prophet's household. It so happened that he stayed longer than usual at the home of Zainab bint Jahsh, where he was offered honey-something he liked very much. Out of jealousy, two other wives (Hafsah and 'Âishah) agreed between themselves to tell the Prophet (peace be upon him), when he visited each of them, that his mouth gave off a bad smell... Eventually, the Prophet made an oath that he would never eat honey again... Both wives are subtly advised to learn from the example of the two believing women mentioned at the end of the sûrah-Mary and Âsiyah, the wife of Pharaoh-and take a lesson from the fate of the wives of Noah and Lot.

sources.name: Shiavault - An Enlightening Commentary into the Light of the Holy Qur'an vol. 18

It addresses an incident within the Prophet's household, in which the Prophet made an oath to give up honey after two of his wives conspired to complain of a bad smell. The surah urges the believers to repent sincerely, protect their families, and take lessons from the examples of righteous and unrighteous women.
